Carmen Li: opened PR 2011 to add a Python SDK example for reading quota headers and wiring into the usage-cost calculator. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2011. Also updated the cost examples to use the new embeddings billing unit (per 1k tokens).
Diego Alvarez: nice. can you make the Python sample defensive? many Dedicated/private installs don't show headers.
Carmen Li: updated snippet to be defensive and included a short helper `safe_quota(headers)` plus a tiny example showing how to convert token counts to billing units. snippet: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_API_KEY'))
resp = client.post('/v1/text/generate', json={'prompt':'hello'})
def safe_quota(hdrs):
    q = hdrs.get('X-Quota-Remaining')
    try:
        return int(q)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None  # unknown quota

quota_left = safe_quota(resp.headers)
if quota_left is None:
    print('quota unknown; check dashboard or use conservative defaults')
else:
    print(f'quota left: {quota_left}')
```
Priya Kapoor: small editorial: prefer "unknown quota" wording instead of "assume unlimited". also add a one-line note that Dedicated returns headers only when routed through the metering proxy.
Carmen Li: done. added a small table mapping deployment -> header availability and a migration note showing old tier names -> new tier names. recalculated pricing worked examples after switching embeddings to per-1k token units.
